title: Grateful Dead Live at Reno Centennial Coliseum on 1982-03-13
lineage: MAC (modified Nakamichi CM-700 mics > Sony TC-D5M on Maxell metal tape) > Nak Dragon playback > Cardas audiophile cables > HHB CDR 800 master CD > Samsung SW-232B extraction (EAC v0.9 beta 4) > tracking (CD Wave) > sector boundary

ai_review.summary: Fast Jerry solos and a blazing Stranger > Franklin's captured on a sparkly though thin audience tape of a wild early‑'82 Reno show.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience (Aud) source that sounds bright and high‑frequency rich but a bit thin in the low end, giving it a decent but not pristine quality. Musically the show erupts with unusually fast Jerry Garcia solos – especially on the Stranger > Franklin's sequence – and even features the only Dear Prudence jam of the tour, delivering a wild early‑set energy that tapers off later in the night.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews highlight strong early performance and unique jams (show quality) but note a drop in energy and an only‑fair audience recording, yielding a moderate overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Sparkly high frequencies with plenty of highs, but thin low end and occasional muddiness; not the best quality but acceptable for an early‑'80s audience tape.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Wild, high‑energy first half that peaks on the Stranger/Franklin's stretch; energy wanes after that and the show takes an odd turn following a law‑enforcement incident.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note unusually fast, high‑tempo solos – “the quickest Jerry I have ever heard” and “Jerry goes absolutely bananas.”
